title: Shaapp Food: A Social Media Services Case Study for a Vyttila, Kochi Kerala Restaurant
storyLead: How Teknoppy shaped the Instagram and Facebook presence of a Kerala-cuisine restaurant near Vyttila Mobility Hub — built around what a hungry local or visitor actually wants to know before walking in.
atAGlance: Instagram and Facebook run as one connected presence, with the same restaurant name, location, and timings on both
Content built around the food people search for: biryani, rice meals, appam, porotta, seafood, and Kerala meat dishes
Over a decade of trading in Vyttila, since 2013, used as a trust point
Opening hours and location made easy to find, since this is what most hungry visitors check first
Every post leads to one clear next step: visiting, calling, or finding the restaurant on the map
aboutParagraphs: Shaapp Food is a restaurant on Kaniyambuzha Road in Vyttila, Kochi, serving South Indian and Kerala cuisine. It has operated since 2013 near the Mobility Hub, and its menu covers what most people expect from a good Kerala meal: biryanis, rice meals, breads such as appam, chapathi, and porotta, vegetarian dishes, seafood, and chicken, beef, duck, and mutton preparations, along with rice and noodle dishes. The restaurant is open from 10 AM to 11 PM on weekdays and from 8 AM to 11 PM on weekends.

Food is one of the most visual and most searched categories on social media. People decide where to eat by looking at dishes, checking how far the place is, and confirming it is open. For a restaurant, the Instagram profile often works as the menu, the map, and the reviews in one place, and it is usually seen before anyone visits the website or calls.

This case study covers the Instagram and Facebook work delivered by Teknoppy: how the profiles are structured, what the content is built around, and how the two platforms support one another. It does not cover the restaurant's kitchen, menu pricing, or service, which belong to Shaapp Food.
challengeLead: Key challenges addressed during the social media engagement:

challenges.title: A long menu needed to be shown in a way people can take in
challenges.description: Biryani, rice meals, seafood, and several meats make for a large menu. Posted without a plan, it looks like a random mix instead of a restaurant known for something.

challenges.title: Over ten years of trading was not visible
challenges.description: Operating since 2013 is a real trust signal in a city full of newer places, but it only helps if visitors can see it quickly.

challenges.title: Hungry visitors check the basics first
challenges.description: Timings, location, and what is on the menu decide whether someone walks in. If those are hard to find, they pick another restaurant.

challenges.title: Vyttila has many places to eat
challenges.description: The Mobility Hub area has steady foot traffic and plenty of competition, so the profile has to give a clear reason to choose this restaurant over the next one.

challenges.title: Instagram and Facebook needed to say the same thing
challenges.description: The two platforms reach different people, but both had to carry identical details so that nobody finds an old timing or a different address.

objectiveLead: Teknoppy was engaged to plan and manage the restaurant's Instagram and Facebook presence so that it helps people find, trust, and visit Shaapp Food. The brief centred on:
objectives: Presenting Kerala dishes clearly, grouped by what people actually search for
Making the 2013 start date and the Vyttila Mobility Hub location easy to notice
Keeping timings, address, and name identical across Instagram, Facebook, and the website
Showing food as it really is, so what a guest sees online matches what is served
Giving every profile and post a clear route to visit or contact the restaurant
approachLead: How Teknoppy built a dish-focused, location-clear social media presence:

approachPillars.title: Content grouped by dish and meal
paragraphs: Instead of posting dishes at random, content is planned around the groups people look for: biryani, Kerala rice meals, appam and porotta with curries, seafood, and meat dishes. A visitor scrolling the profile quickly sees what the restaurant is good at.

approachPillars.title: Years of trading used as a trust signal
paragraphs: The restaurant has served Vyttila since 2013. That history is stated in the profile and returned to in content, because a place that has stayed open for over a decade tells a new visitor something a single photo cannot.

approachPillars.title: Timings and location kept front and centre
paragraphs: Weekday hours of 10 AM to 11 PM and weekend hours from 8 AM to 11 PM, along with the Kaniyambuzha Road address near the Mobility Hub, are written plainly where visitors will see them. Early weekend opening is also worth highlighting for breakfast-style dishes such as appam.

approachPillars.title: Instagram for the food, Facebook for the details
paragraphs: Instagram carries the visuals that make people hungry. Facebook suits fuller descriptions, timings, and information that families and older diners often look for. Both carry the same name and address, so a customer gets the same answer on either one.

approachPillars.title: A profile that works as a quick menu
paragraphs: The profile is set up so a visitor can understand the cuisine, find the restaurant, and contact it without having to ask. Someone deciding where to eat in the next ten minutes should be able to make that choice from the profile alone.

approachPillars.title: Consistent naming across channels
paragraphs: The restaurant appears under the same name, with the same address, across Instagram, Facebook, and its website. This helps customers recognise one business and helps search and map tools connect the profiles to the same place.

deliverables.title: Instagram and Facebook profile setup
deliverables.description: Consistent profiles with the restaurant's name, location, and timings in place on both platforms.

deliverables.title: Dish-based content themes
deliverables.description: Posts grouped around biryani, rice meals, breads, seafood, and meat dishes.

deliverables.title: A trust-led profile
deliverables.description: Operating since 2013 and the Vyttila location presented clearly for new visitors.

deliverables.title: Clear timings and address
deliverables.description: Weekday and weekend hours and the Kaniyambuzha Road location easy to find on both platforms.

deliverables.title: Aligned details across channels
deliverables.description: The same name, address, and timings on Instagram, Facebook, and the website.

deliverables.title: A clear route to visit
deliverables.description: An obvious path from profile or post to the restaurant's location and contact details.

whyMattersParagraphs: People choose a restaurant quickly. They look at a few photos, check where it is and whether it is open, and decide. A profile that answers those questions straight away, and looks like a real, established place, wins that moment. A profile that is unclear or out of date loses it to the next result.

The same clarity helps in search. Search engines and AI answer tools draw on social profiles and business details when they answer questions such as where to get good biryani near Vyttila. When the restaurant's name, address, and timings are stated the same way everywhere, those tools can describe Shaapp Food correctly.

Social media works best alongside a restaurant's website and its listing on maps. Posting to a plan, rather than only when there is something to share, is what makes the profile feel like a place that is open and worth visiting.
